title: Natural Q&A #1
summary: NH's first monthly Natural Q&A covers the danger of steroid-centric advice, standing desks, his ancestry and manga habit, why he started the channel, how much cardio is compatible with bodybuilding, his AI job, his refusal to monetize or coach, his worst injuries, tendinitis, and the pros and cons of fitness culture.
claims: The most dangerous advice in bodybuilding is its source: the culture is steroid-centric, with most advice coming from enhanced lifters or second-hand from them, and it does not apply to naturals
Novices following juiced YouTubers end up disappointed or turn to drugs to get the results that advice implies, which can kill people
The famous sitting-kills study did not control for activity; someone who sits six hours but trains two is healthier than a standing-desk user who never moves
Instead of a standing desk, use a good chair with a lumbar pillow to keep the spine's natural curve, and every 35-45 minutes walk around for 3-4 minutes
If you can, read while walking in a park instead of studying at a desk
He refuses DNA tests like 23andMe because genetic data is private and the databases get sold and accessed by governments
His ancestry is half Spanish, a quarter German and a quarter West African
He has read thousands of manga since age 10 and prefers reading to anime; he usually only watches anime he has already read
He started the channel to express himself and because he believes he has a rare perspective; he posts only when he is adding something new
He learned everything about lifting from YouTube fitness, then experimented to create new knowledge, and now wants to give back so viewers improve on his theories in turn
You can do as much health cardio as you like, but you cannot develop a competitive endurance athlete's traits while also being a high-level bodybuilder
A bodybuilder needs a decent cardiovascular system: if you gas out after four reps you will never accumulate enough tonnage to get big
How much cardio you can do depends on calorie intake, because cardio burns calories that would otherwise build muscle
Cardio also loads muscles and joints, so it has to be factored into frequency and recovery; swimming two hours a day tires the shoulders, upper back and legs
He works in artificial intelligence and has done so for close to two years since his master's
During his master's he ate rice, chicken, spinach and green olives every day for a year and was never bored
His love of repetition is part of why he does well at bodybuilding: he can do the same thing over and over
He has ethical reservations about mixing money with his passion, but would like to train athletes in a fighting sport whose training he finds lacking
The channel is not monetized and probably never will be; once you earn from YouTube you tailor content for clicks and lose your freedom
He will never use admin powers to censor comments; the comment section is an open forum
He does not want to coach; he wants people to learn to program and take responsibility for their own development
His bodybuilding videos are never edited: raw knowledge filmed on weekends
His worst injury ever was a fence spike through his hand while climbing into a basketball court
His worst gym injuries were breaking ribs squatting and busting his left knee; the knee took two years to feel normal and six months before he could squat again
Being told to rest is the worst tendinitis advice: it is a structural problem from poor movement patterns that time eases but cannot solve
Fix tendinitis by training: send blood to the area and build muscle around the tendon, which is how he saved his knee
Lifting can help with depression and anxiety; he got hooked by the waves of endorphins after training and eating
A strong body creates a strong mind; the most miserable people are those unhappy with their bodies
Fitness is prime ground for marketing shortcuts to a better life, which is why YouTube fitness is corrupted, and comparison with others can corrode mental health
Bodybuilding should be tied to spirituality and practised for life, almost like a religion, but it has been desacralized
He started the channel to fight those who corrupt bodybuilding by offering an honest, sincere view of it

what he does for a living
